A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teacher expectancies and students’ self-concepts are related to the students’ perceptions of teacher oral academic feedback, especially positive academic oral feedback.

students’ perceptions of positive and especially negative academic oral feedback are important predictors of teacher expectancies, and that positive academic oral feedback is particularly important in predicting academic self-concept.
teacher expectancies and self-concept are influenced by students’ perceptions of teacher oral academic and nonacademic feedback.
The main takeaway from our work is that

students’ perceptions of teacher oral behavior may influence their academic self-concepts, and that teachers may want to be aware of how their oral feedback may influence their students’ self-concepts.
teachers should provide positive oral feedback to students, and that this feedback should focus on academic domains.
teachers need to provide positive oral feedback to all students, particularly to those who are at risk of developing negative academic self-concept and low expectancies.
